text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- U.S. presidential emissary on the Cyprus dispute Richard Holbrooke is preparing a team to work on the problem, while he is expected on the island at the beginning of August.
- The Health Ministry orders a probe into why corneas taken from a dead donor were never used for transplantation purposes by government doctors.
- Students from capital Nicosia and the western coastal town of Paphos are better at mathematics than students from other districts.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Cyprus protests at Turkish air and sea violations.
- A truce in the taxi drivers strike has been declared as the government takes a new look at issuing more professional licences to drivers.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Era will invest $4 million in index linked funds abroad.
- Record crowds jam McDonald counters as it opens its first store in Larnaca.
- Industrialists repeat calls for the restructure of ministries whose responsibilities overlap with another ministry.
HARAVGHI

- Police suspect the involvement of two other people behind the murder attempt against a Larnaca gambling club owner last month. Three brothers and another man are already in custody on suspicion of involvement.
- The government hints that the purchase of the S300 anti-air missile system from Russia can be used as a bargaining chip during efforts to solve the Cyprus conflict.
PHILELEPHTHEROS

- The National Council, an advisory body on the Cyprus problem, will determine the limits of the Greek Cypriot's negotiating scope during the face-to-face talks slated to start on July 9 in New York between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders.
- The Turkish-occupied areas of Cyprus is used as a link between Israel and Turkey for implementation of their military accords.
SIMERINI

- The government is preparing its position on the territorial aspects of the Cyprus dispute ahead of the July talks, focusing on granting a Turkish Cypriot canton in a federation around 25 percent of Cyprus's territory.
- Lack of discipline is the main problem that the education system in Cyprus faces today, says the school teachers union.
